_doc: Per-tool profile for code-research-first.py.template. The bind step picks the profile matching `tools.code_research` (or `custom` for the 'Other (specify)' case), substitutes placeholders into the template, writes the result to ~/.claude/hooks/<filename_basename>.py, and registers the hook in ~/.claude/settings.json. See SETUP.md § Phase 7a.

required_fields.filename_basename: string — kebab-case basename of the rendered hook (without .py extension). Example: 'tokensave-first', 'ast-grep-first'.
required_fields.bypass_marker: string — exact substring (in a `#` comment) that lets a Bash command through. Convention: <UPPER_SNAKE>_BYPASS:. Example: 'TOKENSAVE_BYPASS:'.
required_fields.detection_mode: enum — one of 'walk_up' or 'cli_available'. Determines how the hook checks if the tool is available for the current project.
required_fields.detection_target: string — for walk_up: relative path of the marker file (e.g. '.tokensave/tokensave.db', 'tags'). For cli_available: the binary name to check via shutil.which (e.g. 'ast-grep', 'src', 'semgrep').
required_fields.sequence_bullets: string — multi-line bulleted text embedded into the rendered hook's stderr block message. JSON-escape newlines as \n; backslashes in regex examples as \\.

optional_fields.url: string|null — tool homepage URL; substituted into {{TOOLS_CODE_RESEARCH_URL}} in skill/CLAUDE.md templates.
optional_fields._skip_install: bool — set true for 'none' to short-circuit the hook-rendering portion of bind. Even with _skip_install: true, the bind step STILL runs orphan cleanup (settings.json de-dup + ask before unlinking stale *-first.py files) so a switch-from-tokensave-to-none correctly removes the prior hook.
optional_fields._uses_user_input: bool — set true for 'custom' to mark the profile as containing nested {{...}} placeholders that the bind step resolves from user input before substituting into the hook template.
optional_fields._note: string — author commentary; ignored by the bind step.
optional_fields._reason: string — alternative to _note for explanatory profile entries (used by 'none'). Treated identically to _note; ignored by the bind step.

tokensave.sequence_bullets:
• Symbol lookup                → tokensave_search <name>
  • 'Where is X / what calls Y'  → tokensave_context <query>
  • Call-graph traversal         → tokensave_callers / tokensave_callees / tokensave_impact
  • File search / locate         → tokensave_files <pattern>
  • Function/class body          → tokensave_body <symbol>

ast-grep.sequence_bullets:
• Symbol-by-name search         → ast-grep run --pattern '<name>' --lang <lang>
  • Structural / AST search      → ast-grep run --pattern '<AST pattern>' --lang <lang>
  • Rule-based scan              → ast-grep scan --rule <rules.yml>
  • File globbing                → ast-grep run --pattern '...' --globs '<pattern>'
  • Reference                    → https://ast-grep.github.io/guide/pattern-syntax.html

sourcegraph.sequence_bullets:
• Symbol search                 → src search 'r:<repo> <name>'
  • Repo-scoped reference search  → src search 'r:<repo> patterntype:literal <name>'
  • Cross-repo search             → src search 'r:.* <name>'
  • File pattern                  → src search 'r:<repo> type:file f:<pattern>'
  • Code intelligence (LSIF/SCIP) → instances with code intel expose go-to-definition / find-references via raw GraphQL queries through 'src api'. Check your instance's docs for the exact query shape.

ctags.sequence_bullets:
• Generate tags file            → ctags -R -f tags . (regenerate after edits; cheap)
  • Symbol lookup (Universal)     → readtags -t tags -e -p '<prefix>'  (canonical; insert '-' separator only for dash-prefixed names)
  • Symbol lookup (any ctags)     → grep -E '^<name>\b' tags  (use # CTAGS_BYPASS: <reason> marker — this is the canonical lookup, not a fallback)
  • File globbing                 → use Glob; ctags doesn't index file names
  • Reference                     → https://docs.ctags.io

semgrep.sequence_bullets:
• Pattern search                → semgrep --pattern '<pattern>' --lang <lang>
  • Symbol-by-name               → semgrep --pattern '<name>' --lang <lang>
  • Rule-based scan              → semgrep --config <rules.yml>
  • Auto-config registry         → semgrep --config auto (downloads relevant rule packs)
  • File globbing                → use Glob; Semgrep doesn't index file names

none._reason: User selected `none` for tools.code_research. No PreToolUse hook is installed. CLAUDE.md, the /find skill, and the read-before-writing rule resolve to the Grep/Glob/Read sequence without any enforcement layer.

custom.sequence_bullets:
• Refer to {{TOOLS_CODE_RESEARCH_URL}} for the canonical command sequence.
  • The bind step writes this stub; refine the sequence bullets in ~/.claude/hooks/{{TOOLS_CODE_RESEARCH_NAME_KEBAB}}-first.py to match the tool's actual CLI surface.
custom._note: Custom code-research tool. The bind step computes filename_basename, bypass_marker, and detection_target from the user-supplied name using these transformations: NAME_KEBAB = name.lower() with non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to single '-'; NAME_UPPER_SNAKE = name.upper() with non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to single '_'. The resulting hook is a stub — the user should refine the sequence_bullets to match their tool's CLI.
